name: EditEngine
summary: Shopify bulk product editor (by Profitonium): filter products by collection, tag, vendor or status, then change prices, titles, tags, inventory, SEO fields and metafields in one run, with a preview first, scheduled runs for sales and an undo history. Plans are gated on products per task.
best_for: Shopify merchants with hundreds or thousands of products who change prices, tags, SEO fields or metafields in bulk and want a preview and an undo before anything goes live
skip_if: you only edit a handful of products at a time, which Shopify's own bulk editor already covers, or you are not comfortable granting an app broad access to your store data
honest_knock: Undo covers supported in-app edits only: deletes are permanent, and a spreadsheet import is only reversible if you kept the original export yourself. Percentage price changes stack: running the same edit twice applies it twice. The developer's terms give no refunds for partial billing periods, and the app asks for wide access to the store, including products, inventory, orders and customers.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · per month, per store per 30 days on the Shopify App Store listing, billed in USD
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-26 on the EditEngine listing in the Shopify App Store; the listing says all charges are billed in USD, every 30 days) EditEngine has a free plan and three paid plans, and every plan allows unlimited bulk edit, import and export tasks. What changes is how many products and collections one task may touch. Free: 100 products and 5 collections per task, with undo and unlimited Import Advanced. Basic: $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, 500 products and 10 collections per task, plus metafields export. Standard: $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year, 10,000 products and 100 collections per task, and scheduled bulk edits. Pro: $49.99 a month or $499.99 a year, unlimited products and collections per task. The annual prices save 17%. Partner development stores get unlimited use for free. An optional Backup add-on is listed as $6.99 to $59.99 a month; the listing does not break that range down.

compare_with.name: Shopify's built-in bulk editor
compare_with.why: the bulk editor in Shopify Admin costs nothing extra and lets you edit selected products in a spreadsheet view. EditEngine has to earn its price with rule-based changes across filtered products, a preview of every change, scheduled runs for sales and launches, CSV and XLSX import, and an undo history

method: Development store (Shopify plan Basic): installed the app and ran a storewide 5 percent price increase with preview, applied it to 19 products and undid it

claims.plan: Unlimited development store plan; no paid plan selectable
claims.comparability: Dossier preview wording versus the preview card and a plain calculation on the example prices.
claims.buying_consequence: You see the new prices before anything is saved.

claims.observed: About 2.5 minutes and 8 clicks after the start of the install the summary said 19 of 19 products processed in 8.0 seconds with No errors.
claims.plan: Unlimited development store plan; no paid plan selectable
claims.comparability: Dossier speed wording versus the Edit Summary of one 19 product development store; the storefront was not opened.
claims.buying_consequence: A storewide price change on 19 products took 8 seconds once the preview was approved; whether the prices in the store changed was not checked.

claims.claim: Bulk Edit Reverted. 19 product restored to previous state

claims.plan: Unlimited development store plan; no paid plan selectable
claims.comparability: Dossier undo wording versus the app status after the undo; no product prices were opened.
claims.buying_consequence: The app reports a full undo; the restored prices were not checked in the store.

claims.observed: The Select your plan window shows a Free plan at $0 /month and a button Try Free Plan, which was greyed out on the development store, so the Free plan limits could not be tried.
claims.plan: Unlimited development store plan; no paid plan selectable
claims.comparability: Listing wording versus a greyed out button on one development store.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested EditEngine (Bulk Product Editor in the app) on a Shopify development store: the install, a storewide 5 percent price increase with a preview of old and new prices, applying it to 19 products in 8.0 seconds, undoing it, the Select your plan window with greyed out buttons and the uninstall of the app. Nothing was paid, no approval screen was reached and the prices in the store were not checked after the undo. Install: the app is called EditEngine Bulk Product Editor in the App Store listing (English; Free plan available, 4.9 from 162 reviews, Built for Shopify, developer Profitonium), Bulk Product Editor in the install dialog and EditEngine: Bulk Product Editor in the app. The first install attempt at about 13:24 used the wrong form and had no effect; the real install started at about 13:24:40 in our own tab. The dialog Install app warned that Bulk Product Editor doesn't support market-driven shipping and asked for View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, custom data, Shopify admin, other data); the listing also names View customer data and customers, orders, discounts and store credit. The app opened at once without a payment, plan choice, account or demo, with Products 19, Bulk edits 0, Exports 0 and Current plan: Unlimited. Core action, a bulk price change with preview, apply and undo: the start screen offers Ask EditEngine with the line You review a preview before anything is saved. We chose the example Increase all prices by 5% and sent it. The chat Storewide five percent price increase read the request, checked the fields and showed the preview card Raise price by 5% for All products, 19 products and all variants, with examples such as The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard $949.95 to $997.45, four Gift Card amounts and The Minimal Snowboard $885.95 to $930.25 (all agree with a plain 5 percent increase) and Show all 10 preview examples. The card says Nothing changes until you click Apply. You can undo it afterwards. and shows Apply to 19 products, Adjust, Cancel and Preview valid until 01:40 PM. Apply started the edit; after Refresh the job said Completed and a toast said Bulk edit finished. The summary says Processed 19/19 product in 8.0s, No errors, 1:26 PM, Action: IncreaseByPercent. The result was visible about 2.5 minutes after the start of the install (about 13:24:40 to 13:27) in 8 clicks (Install, confirm Install, the example sentence, Send, Review and apply, Apply to 19 products, Refresh status, View results); the edit itself took 8.0 seconds. Undo: Undo Edit opened the dialog Undo bulk edit (Are you sure you want to undo this bulk edit? This will revert all changes made to 19 product.) with the notice This action cannot be undone., and after Confirm Undo the summary said Bulk Edit Reverted, 19 product restored to previous state, with the button Reverted. The prices in the store itself were not looked at after the undo. Plans: Upgrade opens Select your plan with a switch Monthly or Annual (Save 17%). It says Your current plan: Unlimited and Development store: Free unlimited access while your store is in development. When it moves to a paid Shopify plan, you'll pick from the plans below. On Annual the cards show Basic $8.33 /month ($99.99 /year), Standard $16.67 /month ($199.99 /year), Pro $41.67 /month ($499.99 /year) and Free $0 /month. Basic allows 500 products and 10 collections per task and has no scheduled bulk edits (crossed out); Standard allows 10,000 products and 100 collections and has scheduled edits; Pro is unlimited with scheduled edits; all plans list Undo and rollback edits and Export metafields. An add-on, automatic daily backups, costs $6.99/month and works with every plan. The App Store shows monthly prices of $9.99, $19.99 and $49.99 and the same yearly amounts; the app shows a monthly equivalent on the Annual view, and the Monthly view was set but not captured. Checkout: the buttons Try Basic Plan, Try Standard Plan, Try Pro Plan and Try Free Plan were greyed out on the development store, so no Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, nothing was approved and no card was asked. Cancelling: no subscription existed (the development store has the Unlimited plan). The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of Bulk Product Editor and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Bulk Product Editor? says you will no longer be able to use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted; the Uninstall button only works after a reason is chosen (Testing multiple apps). No picture of that dialog was kept. Not tested: the plans Basic, Standard and Pro, scheduled edits, deleting products, import and export, the Backup add-on, the connection with Claude, ChatGPT or Sidekick, the storefront preview, and the product prices in the store after the undo. Clean up: the test edit was undone (status Reverted); the app was uninstalled after the test with the reason Testing multiple apps and is gone from the installed apps; no theme change was saved. Other apps were not touched. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The install dialog warns that the app does not support market-driven shipping, the app name differs between the listing, the install dialog and the app, the Try plan buttons are greyed out on a development store, the app shows a monthly equivalent on the Annual view while the listing shows monthly prices, and the first install attempt had to be repeated.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested EditEngine (Bulk Product Editor in the app) on a Shopify development store: the install, a storewide 5 percent price increase with a preview of old and new prices, applying it to 19 products in 8.0 seconds, undoing it, the Select your plan window with greyed out buttons and the uninstall of the app. Nothing was paid, no approval screen was reached and the prices in the store were not checked after the undo. Install: the app is called EditEngine Bulk Product Editor in the App Store listing (English; Free plan available, 4.9 from 162 reviews, Built for Shopify, developer Profitonium), Bulk Product Editor in the install dialog and EditEngine: Bulk Product Editor in the app. The first install attempt at about 13:24 used the wrong form and had no effect; the real install started at about 13:24:40 in our own tab. The dialog Install app warned that Bulk Product Editor doesn't support market-driven shipping and asked for View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, custom data, Shopify admin, other data); the listing also names View customer data and customers, orders, discounts and store credit. The app opened at once without a payment, plan choice, account or demo, with Products 19, Bulk edits 0, Exports 0 and Current plan: Unlimited. Core action, a bulk price change with preview, apply and undo: the start screen offers Ask EditEngine with the line You review a preview before anything is saved. We chose the example Increase all prices by 5% and sent it. The chat Storewide five percent price increase read the request, checked the fields and showed the preview card Raise price by 5% for All products, 19 products and all variants, with examples such as The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard $949.95 to $997.45, four Gift Card amounts and The Minimal Snowboard $885.95 to $930.25 (all agree with a plain 5 percent increase) and Show all 10 preview examples. The card says Nothing changes until you click Apply. You can undo it afterwards. and shows Apply to 19 products, Adjust, Cancel and Preview valid until 01:40 PM. Apply started the edit; after Refresh the job said Completed and a toast said Bulk edit finished. The summary says Processed 19/19 product in 8.0s, No errors, 1:26 PM, Action: IncreaseByPercent. The result was visible about 2.5 minutes after the start of the install (about 13:24:40 to 13:27) in 8 clicks (Install, confirm Install, the example sentence, Send, Review and apply, Apply to 19 products, Refresh status, View results); the edit itself took 8.0 seconds. Undo: Undo Edit opened the dialog Undo bulk edit (Are you sure you want to undo this bulk edit? This will revert all changes made to 19 product.) with the notice This action cannot be undone., and after Confirm Undo the summary said Bulk Edit Reverted, 19 product restored to previous state, with the button Reverted. The prices in the store itself were not looked at after the undo. Plans: Upgrade opens Select your plan with a switch Monthly or Annual (Save 17%). It says Your current plan: Unlimited and Development store: Free unlimited access while your store is in development. When it moves to a paid Shopify plan, you'll pick from the plans below. On Annual the cards show Basic $8.33 /month ($99.99 /year), Standard $16.67 /month ($199.99 /year), Pro $41.67 /month ($499.99 /year) and Free $0 /month. Basic allows 500 products and 10 collections per task and has no scheduled bulk edits (crossed out); Standard allows 10,000 products and 100 collections and has scheduled edits; Pro is unlimited with scheduled edits; all plans list Undo and rollback edits and Export metafields. An add-on, automatic daily backups, costs $6.99/month and works with every plan. The App Store shows monthly prices of $9.99, $19.99 and $49.99 and the same yearly amounts; the app shows a monthly equivalent on the Annual view, and the Monthly view was set but not captured. Checkout: the buttons Try Basic Plan, Try Standard Plan, Try Pro Plan and Try Free Plan were greyed out on the development store, so no Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, nothing was approved and no card was asked. Cancelling: no subscription existed (the development store has the Unlimited plan). The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of Bulk Product Editor and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Bulk Product Editor? says you will no longer be able to use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted; the Uninstall button only works after a reason is chosen (Testing multiple apps). No picture of that dialog was kept. Not tested: the plans Basic, Standard and Pro, scheduled edits, deleting products, import and export, the Backup add-on, the connection with Claude, ChatGPT or Sidekick, the storefront preview, and the product prices in the store after the undo. Clean up: the test edit was undone (status Reverted); the app was uninstalled after the test with the reason Testing multiple apps and is gone from the installed apps; no theme change was saved. Other apps were not touched. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The install dialog warns that the app does not support market-driven shipping, the app name differs between the listing, the install dialog and the app, the Try plan buttons are greyed out on a development store, the app shows a monthly equivalent on the Annual view while the listing shows monthly prices, and the first install attempt had to be repeated.
